issues.question: Does high Bay water get into Berkeley's storm drains, and do tide gates keep it out?

responsibleAgencies.name: City of Berkeley Public Works
responsibleAgencies.role: Holds storm drain records: its 2023 storm work orders are published (D5), and the pipe, outfall and gate records are not in the City's open data (D2, DATA_INVENTORY.md).

responsibleAgencies.name: City of Berkeley City Clerk (public records requests)
responsibleAgencies.role: Receives public records requests through the NextRequest portal, by form, in person or by mail (D10).

issues.decision: No decision is pending on record. The open question is a records gap: which outfalls have tide gates, where they are, how high their pipes sit and whether the gates work.

alternatives.label: Ask for the records
alternatives.detail: A public records request for the outfall inventory, gate locations and condition, invert elevations, drainage studies and maintenance records. It would replace the model's assumed open outfalls with what is there.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Costs a request and staff time; the City may hold some records only on paper or not at all.

alternatives.label: Look first at what is already released
alternatives.detail: NextRequest shows past requests and the documents released in response (D10). The City's utility as-built drawing request form is for contractors and engineers (D10).
alternatives.tradeoffs: Free and fast; may find nothing on outfalls or gates.

alternatives.label: Watch the drains at a king tide
alternatives.detail: Photos of storm drain grates near the shore around this winter's highest tides (the king tide field guide) show whether water comes up, at that tide.
alternatives.tradeoffs: One tide, one place at a time; says nothing about a storm tide or rain.

alternatives.label: Do nothing for now
alternatives.detail: Keep the explorer's two assumptions side by side, gates open and gates closed, and say which one the evidence supports when records appear.
alternatives.tradeoffs: The drain results stay a range between two assumptions.

evidenceGaps.why: The model places one outfall per watershed at the cell nearest open water (D3).
Decide at what Bay level water enters each pipe and how long the tide holds it shut (DATA_INVENTORY.md).
Which outfalls have gates, and whether they work, decides whether the teal ground can fill at all (D6, C9).
The model assumes every inlet connects to its watershed's outfall (D6).
The 2023 work orders follow rain, not high tides (D5).

evidenceGaps.item: Aquatic Park lagoon levels and gate settings
evidenceGaps.why: Whether the lagoon follows the Bay at a storm tide (D9).
